ROBOBENCH: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brain. arXiv.
creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang (Peking University; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence; Fudan University; University of Science and Technology Beijing; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics)
description: RoboBench is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It covers five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs, built from real robotic data and in-house collection.
name: RoboBench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper describes a two-stage quality control process: data filtering during construction and post-construction validation. Twenty professionally trained annotators conducted quality inspections for linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness, and a majority-vote strategy was used to remove items all models solved correctly and manually review/correct items all models failed.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were produced using both machine and human procedures. Implicit instructions were obtained by rewriting explicit instructions using LLMs; perception data include GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes; planning annotations were generated by Gemini and refined by human annotators; affordance frames were annotated with static, dynamic, and mobile affordances; failure data include expert labels for execution failures and synthesized planning failures by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that existing benchmarks suffer from a simulation-to-reality gap and states that RoboBench combines large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection to narrow that gap. It also contrasts explicit versus implicit instruction formulations to test grounding of indirect human intent, reflecting a design choice to avoid over-reliance on explicit instruction bias.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. It combines large-scale real-world robotic datasets with curated in-house collection across instruction, perception, planning, affordance, and failure-analysis tasks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data include open-source and in-house robotic data such as real robot videos, frame sequences, multi-view scenes, and data from large-scale real-world robotic datasets used to construct the benchmark.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reveals that current models struggle particularly with implicit instruction grounding, robotic-view recognition, temporal grounding, complex planning, affordance prediction, and execution-level failure diagnosis. For planning failures, the paper notes that real-world planning failure data were lacking, so planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection transformations include rewriting explicit instructions into implicit instructions using LLMs, standardizing data into multiple-choice QA, extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs, mapping step descriptions into predefined function templates, sampling representative frames for affordance annotation, and synthesizing planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The paper describes preprocessing and filtering steps including image-quality and task-validity filtering, task-specific exclusion rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks, extracting frame sequences as standardized inputs, and standardizing multiple data sources into QA formats and structured action/function representations.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for systematic evaluation of multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation, including evaluation of instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLMs/VLMs were used in the annotation pipeline, including LLMs for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit ones, GPT for generating functional properties and distractors, Gemini for segmented video steps and structured planning annotations, and MLLMs/detection models in the dataset construction pipeline.
